newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-NORMAN EXTENDS LEAD AS WOODS IMPROVES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN EXTENDS LEAD AS WOODS IMPROVES.

text.p: World number one Greg Norman extended his lead to four shots in the A$1 million (US$800,000) Australian Open on Saturday.
Tiger Woods beat par for the first time but was 11 shots behind the Australian after the third round. Both fired one-under-par 71s.
Norman's lead was all the more impressive after he was one of 39 players who were unable to complete their second rounds on Friday because of rain and high winds.

Norman resumed his round at 7 a.m. with two holes to play but dropped a shot to card a 73. He briefly handed the lead to Sweden's Klas Eriksson, who completed his three remaining holes for a 71 to go one ahead.
Eriksson's advantage was short-lived, the Swede returning to the course to fire a 76 to put him on 215, worth second place but four behind Norman.
The Australian and the Swede were the only two players under par for the tournament.
Defending champion Norman would not be drawn into comparisons with April's U.S. Masters, where he held a six-shot lead going into the final round but lost.
"It was just a very long day in tough conditions," Norman said.
"You are more tired mentally than physically because playing three straight days in this stuff really beats your head up pretty good."
Woods, who picked up a cold in Friday's miserable weather, did not write off his chances despite being so far behind.
"If I shoot low enough, who knows," Woods said. "It depends on the wind, too. If it's blowing like this even par might win but, either way, I am going to have to go low."
Norman doubted Woods confidence. When asked if he thought the talented young American was out of contention, Norman replied: "With the weather like this, I would say yes."
